questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was in the EU, that the city had a lot to offer in terms of culture, learning a new language

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay but there was a lot to stay updated on and sometimes I was affraid of missing important deadlines.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus Association has been so great both in terms of arranging social welcome activities and helping out with practical questions regarding life in the city and the university. Also the university send a handbook and made an information webinar which was very helpful

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The only thing missing would be a tour around campus. I was quite lost in the beginning

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy especially since I had a friend who knows what facebook groups and web pages to use.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived in an airbnb for the first 2,5 weeks in order to explore the city and find out what areas I liked before choosing an apartment. It worked so well also because that way I could see the apartment where I spent the rest of my stay with my own eyes. I recommend doing that.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I don't know since I did not use it.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Signing up for courses was difficult because my login did not work and the procedure was not very logic. Fortunately, someone from the administration helped my and the problem was quickly solved.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is more than a year since I did it so I do not really remember the difference between the process at KU and the one at my host institution

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We received a handbook and the administration was quite easy to reach.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make use of the information you receive and if you are still in doubt just contact the administration and they will help you. Also, ask clearly what deadlines you should be aware of.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some classes were really great but some were very unorganised. The quality was very different from course to course

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took a mix between BA and MA courses and that worked really fine

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. Participation in class and through micro tasks, exercises, upload of reading reports and group presentation was much more a central part of the course and also counted in the final grade. It gave me more work throughout the semester but made the final exam period much easier. Also, I feel like I learned more from having to do all the exercises, but I would not have been able to engage so much if it was at UCPH because I work too much in my student position.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Gender politics; Demography, Society and Policy in Europe; International Economics; Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability; Digital Economy, Data and Society.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Digital Economy, Data and Society: Very good professor and interesting content that I have not learned about at UCPH
International Economics: Very good teachers, I found it extremely interesting and learned a lot

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing really

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Rent could definitely have been cheaper, but I wanted to live in a more expensive area in a really nice apartment, so for what I have, the price is good, but others can easily find a good and cheaper place.
It has been cheaper to go out for dinner and partying than I expected which has really been great.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not use it much. I think it is a shame that the sports teams are only for advanced levels because it would be a good way to socialize.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports teams such as volleyball, football etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Don't know

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on trips out of the city. The country has so much to offer and it is easy to get around by train. Also, speak with locals and get their recommendations, it is the best way of getting off the beaten track

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy once you get used to the fact that nothing starts and no one arrives on time

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Start with the ones in your class, use the breaks to speak with them and ask them if they want to have lunch.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That no one is on time, that a lot is a little unorganized and could be done more efficiently and smarter. It was frustrating at times

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That no one plan too far in the future which makes spontaneous things possible. Also, that enjoying life and social encounters are prioritized over efficiency. I think we could learn a lot from that in our stressed, scheduled, efficient part of the world.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. Reach out to someone who has been on exchange there in order to get their tips and recommendations. 2. Participate in the welcome program as much as possible as it is very much where friendships are established. 3. Don't do it for the courses, do it for the culture, the experience, the food etc. Don't spend too much time on the exams and classes, just enjoy your stay (generally, professors are quite generous on the grades anyway)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't know

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Just the total experience of living in this city and get to know it, its culture and so many good people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That a lot of friends and family from Denmark wanted to visit. It was of course so nice but at the same time it could also be too much and distract me from being with the people I got to know here.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
